The '''Operations Support Branch''' ('''OSB''') is a unit of the cyber-intelligence division of the [[Central Intelligence Agency]] (CIA).<ref name="NY22">{{Cite magazine |last=Keefe |first=Patrick Radden |author-link=Patrick Radden Keefe |date=2022-06-06 |title=The Surreal Case of a C.I.A. Hacker's Revenge |url=https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2022/06/13/the-surreal-case-of-a-cia-hackers-revenge |magazine=[[The New Yorker]] |accessdate=8 June 2022}}</ref> It is located on the ninth floor of a secret facility in the suburbs of northern Virginia, west of [[Washington, D.C.]]<ref name=NY22/> [[Patrick Radden Keefe]] described the OSB as the CIA's "secret hacker unit, in which a cadre of élite engineers create cyberweapons" in a June 2022 article for ''[[The New Yorker]]''.<ref name=NY22/>

The OSB specializes in [[Physical access|physical access operations]] in which 'physical access' is gained to electronic devices owned by high value individual targets such as foreign government officials and terrorists.<ref name=NY22/> The OSB is able to quickly develop tools that can be utilised in cyberintelligence missions at short notice.<ref name=NY22/>

According to anonymous witnesses who testified at [[Joshua Schulte]]'s trial, the OSB was filled with workspace pranks, like stealing coworkers' things, name calling, shoving matches, rubber band and [[Nerf Blaster|Nerf gun]] wars. Asked if she was aware of this, the former head of CIA's Center for Cyber Intelligence Bonnie Stith said she was not.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Hong |first=Nicole |date=2020-02-17 |title=Life of a C.I.A. Coder: Nerf Guns, Pranks and Fat Jokes |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/02/17/nyregion/joshua-schulte-cia-wikileaks.html |access-date=2022-07-30 |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

The employees of the OSB numbered about a dozen in the 2010s.<ref name=NY22/> Radden Keefe described the extreme secrecy of the OSB at this period as resulting in staff unable to " ... take work home, or talk with anyone on the outside about what they did all day. Their office was a classified sanctum, a locked vault. Like the crew of a submarine, they forged strong bonds—and strong antagonisms".<ref name=NY22/> The software engineer [[Joshua Schulte]] was employed by the OSB from 2010 to 2016. He was convicted of being the leaker of the [[Vault 7]] documents which detail electronic surveillance and [[cyber warfare]] tools developed by the CIA.<ref name=NY22/><ref>{{Cite press release |title=Statement Of U.S. Attorney Damian Williams On The Espionage Conviction Of Ex-CIA Programmer Joshua Adam Schulte |date=2022-07-13 |publisher=[[United States Department of Justice]] |url=https://www.justice.gov/usao-sdny/pr/statement-us-attorney-damian-williams-espionage-conviction-ex-cia-programmer-joshua |language=en |last1=Williams |first1=Damian |access-date=2022-07-29 |author-link1=Damian Williams (lawyer)}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Shanahan |first=Ed |date=2022-07-13 |title=Ex-C.I.A. Engineer Convicted in Biggest Theft Ever of Agency Secrets |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/07/13/nyregion/cia-engineer-joshua-schulte-theft-convicted.html |access-date=2022-07-29 |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-07-14 |title=Ex-CIA engineer convicted over massive data leak |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/7/14/ex-cia-engineer-joshua-schulte-convicted-of-largest-data |access-date=2022-07-29 |publisher=[[Al Jazeera English]] |language=en}}</ref> Schulte was nicknamed '[[Voldemort]]' during his time at the OSB.<ref name=NY22/> The leak and publication of the Vault 7 documents was a significant blow to the CIA, a senior official likened it to the 'digital' equivalent of the [[attack on Pearl Harbor]] in its scope and fallout.<ref name=NY22/>
